findings.explanation: resolvePageCredential() decrypts the stored page credential (secret, e.g. Messenger page access token) and logs its raw plaintext value to console.log on every successful resolution. Anyone with log access (Railway logs, log aggregator, etc.) can read live page access tokens. Contrast with core/webhook.js and core/admin/session.js, which consistently hash identifiers via pageRef()/shopRef() (core/utils/log-refs.js) and never log raw secrets/tokens — this line is the one place a raw secret reaches the log stream. No redact call wraps `secret` here. Fix: drop `secret` from the log line entirely (log only shop/credential id, e.g. via shopRef(normalizedShopId)).
